ai.literal: Thinking 'it has difficulty', not being discouraged is required; greatness effort will give.
ai.translation: One should not lose heart thinking a task is too difficult; for earnest effort will yield the greatness to accomplish it.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்வது கடினம் என்று நினைத்துச் சோர்வடையாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்; முயற்சி அச்செயலை முடிப்பதற்கான பெருமையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises learners and doers never to shrink back from a task by assuming it is too difficult or impossible. The word 'அசாவாமை' means not fainting or not losing heart under the weight of a challenge. The poet emphasizes that 'முயற்சி' (effort) is the key driver that brings 'பெருமை' (greatness or the capacity to succeed). By persisting with effort, even the most daunting tasks are rendered achievable, transforming difficulty into triumph.

ai.literal: In action, avoid ruining the action; the world has abandoned those who leave their work unfinished, just like those who have completely failed.
ai.translation: Avoid slacking or ruining an undertaking while in the midst of it; the world will abandon those who leave their work incomplete, just as it abandons those who are completely ruined.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்யும்போது சோர்வடைந்து அச்செயலைக் கெடுத்துவிடுவதைத் தவிர்க்க வேண்டும். அவ்வாறு செய்யாமல் வேலையை அரைகுறையாக விட்டுவிடுபவர்களை, முற்றிலும் அழிந்துபோனவர்களை உலகம் கைவிடுவது போல, உலகமும் கைவிட்டுவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of completing any undertaken task without slacking or leaving it unfinished. The poet advises that once an action is started ('வினைக்கண்'), one must guard against ('ஓம்பல்') ruining it ('வினைகெடல்') through laziness or loss of enthusiasm. If a person leaves their work incomplete ('வினைக்குறை'), the world will abandon them ('தீர்ந்தன்று உலகு') just as it completely ignores and abandons those who have already failed or lost everything ('தீர்ந்தாரின்'). Success lies not just in starting, but in carrying a task through to its absolute completion.

ai.literal: In the noble quality called persevering effort, rests indeed the noble pride called benevolence.
ai.translation: The noble pride of being able to help others rests entirely upon the high quality of persevering effort.
ai.modern: முயற்சி என்று சொல்லப்படும் உயர்ந்த குணத்தில்தான், பிறருக்கு உதவி செய்தல் என்று சொல்லப்படும் பெருமிதம் நிலைபெற்றுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the relationship between effort (tāḷāṇmai) and benevolence (vēḷāṇmai). The poet states that the proud privilege of being able to help others (vēḷāṇmai ennuñ cerukku) can only abide or be sustained within the noble quality of relentless effort and perseverance (tāḷāṇmai ennum takaimai). Without hard work and the wealth it brings, one cannot experience the joy of generosity. Thus, active exertion is the foundation of all charity.

ai.literal: The benevolence of one who lacks industriousness, like the swordsmanship in the hand of a hermaphrodite, will fail.
ai.translation: The benevolence of one who lacks industriousness will fail, just like the swordsmanship in the hand of a hermaphrodite.
ai.modern: முயற்சி இல்லாதவனுடைய கொடைத்தன்மை, பேடியின் கையில் உள்ள வாளின் வீரம் போல வீணாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights that noble intentions are useless without the practical means to execute them. The desire to help others (வேளாண்மை) requires wealth, which can only be earned through hard work and industriousness (தாளாண்மை). If a person lacks this industriousness, their desire to be charitable is compared to a sword in the hand of a hermaphrodite (பேடி கை வாளாண்மை). Just as a sword is useless in the hands of someone who cannot fight, charity is impossible for someone who does not work to acquire the means to give.

ai.literal: Pleasure he who desires not, work he who desires, his relations' suffering having wiped away, propping up pillar.
ai.translation: He who does not seek personal pleasure but desires only to do his work will become a supporting pillar that wipes away the suffering of his kin.
ai.modern: இன்பத்தை விரும்பாமல் தன் கடமையாகிய செயலைச் செய்ய விரும்புகின்றவன், தன் சுற்றத்தாரின் துன்பத்தைத் துடைத்து அவர்களைத் தாங்கி நிற்கும் தூண் ஆவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the noble quality of a person dedicated to effort and duty. One who disregards personal ease and instead finds joy in hard work becomes a source of strength for their family and friends. By actively working, they wipe away the distress of their relatives and stand firm as a supportive pillar, bearing the weight of their community's welfare.

ai.literal: Effort wealth will create; lack of effort poverty having introduced will leave.
ai.translation: Effort brings about prosperity, whereas the lack of effort will usher in poverty and leave one destitute.
ai.modern: முயற்சி செல்வத்தை உண்டாக்கும்; முயற்சி செய்யாமல் இருப்பது வறுமையைக் கொண்டு வந்து சேர்த்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the outcomes of industriousness and laziness. The word 'திரு' refers to wealth and prosperity, which are actively generated by effort ('முயற்சி'). On the other hand, the absence of effort ('முயற்றின்மை') inevitably introduces 'இன்மை', which here means poverty and destitution. The auxiliary verb 'விடும்' emphasizes the certainty of this negative outcome, warning the reader that inaction leads directly to ruin.

ai.literal: In laziness, she, the dark goddess of misfortune, they say; of him who has no laziness, in the effort, he, she of the lotus.
ai.translation: They say the dark goddess of misfortune dwells in laziness, while the Goddess of the lotus resides in the active effort of the one who is free from laziness.
ai.modern: சோம்பல் உடையவரிடத்தில் கரிய மூதேவி தங்குவாள் என்றும், சோம்பல் இல்லாதவனுடைய முயற்சியிடத்தில் தாமரையில் வீற்றிருக்கும் திருமகள் தங்குவாள் என்றும் கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the consequences of laziness and active effort using powerful symbolic figures. The poet states that 'மாமுகடி' (the dark goddess of misfortune and poverty) makes her home within laziness ('மடியுள்'). Conversely, 'தாமரையினாள்' (the goddess of the lotus, representing wealth and prosperity) resides within the persistent effort ('தாளுள்') of a person who is free from laziness ('மடியிலான்'). Through this imagery, the couplet teaches that sloth brings ruin, while hard work naturally attracts prosperity.

ai.literal: Lack of destiny is not a disgrace to anyone; knowing what is to be known, lack of effort is disgrace.
ai.translation: Lacking favorable fortune or natural endowment is no disgrace to anyone; but lacking effort, after knowing what needs to be done, is a true disgrace.
ai.modern: விதி அல்லது நல்வினை இல்லாமல் இருப்பது யாருக்கும் பழி ஆகாது; ஆனால், செய்ய வேண்டியவற்றை அறிந்து முயற்சி செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே பழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts external circumstances with personal responsibility. The word 'poṟi' refers to fate, luck, or natural physical endowment; the poet asserts that lacking these is not a disgrace because they are beyond a person's control. However, 'āḷviṉai iṉmai' (the lack of effort) is a genuine disgrace. The phrase 'aṟivu aṟintu' emphasizes that one must first acquire the necessary knowledge of how to perform a task, and then apply effort; failing to try despite knowing what to do is where the real blame lies.

ai.literal: Even if by fate it is not possible, effort will give the wages for its own body-wearying labor.
ai.translation: Even if destiny makes a task impossible, one's honest effort will still yield the wages due for the physical labor spent.
ai.modern: விதியினால் ஒரு செயல் முடியாமல் போனாலும், முயற்சி செய்வதனால் ஏற்படும் உடம்பின் வருத்தத்திற்கு ஏற்ற பலனை அந்த முயற்சி தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of personal effort over fate. Even when external circumstances or destiny make the ultimate goal unattainable, the physical exertion put into the task does not go to waste. The effort itself guarantees a return proportional to the bodily pain and labor endured. This teaches that while success might sometimes be blocked by factors beyond control, honest labor always yields its own reward and is never entirely in vain.

ai.literal: Even fate, the back they will see, discouragement without, without delaying, those who strive.
ai.translation: Those who strive unremittingly without discouragement will see even fate turn its back and retreat.
ai.modern: மனச்சோர்வு இல்லாமல், காலம் தாழ்த்தாமல் முயற்சி செய்பவர்கள், விதியையும் புறமுதுகு காட்டி ஓடச் செய்வர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the power of relentless human effort over destiny. The poet asserts that even fate, which is often considered insurmountable, can be defeated and made to turn its back in retreat. This victory is achieved by those who labor without discouragement and without delaying or slacking. The key term 'உப்பக்கம்' literally means 'the back', symbolizing defeat, showing that persistent effort can overcome even the most adverse preordained circumstances.
